evidence: Single package (pyexcel_xlsx) with clear internal modules (book.py, xlsxr.py, xlsxw.py) indicating logical separation of concerns
No explicit service boundaries or inter-process communication patterns — all logic resides in one distribution package
Well-defined module responsibilities: xlsxr for reading, xlsxw for writing, book for workbook-level operations
Heavy use of inheritance and interface-like base classes (ISheet, IReader, IWriter) from pyexcel_io, suggesting cohesive modular design
Tests organized in a single tests directory with clear fixture-based structure, supporting modular testing
Directory depth of 3 reflects typical module hierarchy, not service or microservice decomposition
Shared dependencies (openpyxl, pyexcel_io) across modules indicates single deployment unit
risks: Potential for tight coupling between reader/writer components if abstractions are not enforced strictly
Limited scalability if monolithic design grows without further decoupling
No deployment or scaling granularity — entire module must be redeployed for any change
